title: Exploring the assessment of post-cardiac valve surgery pulmonary complication risks through the integration of wearable continuous physiological and clinical data.
summary: The open-access primary article prospectively studies 100 cardiac-valve surgery patients with wearable nocturnal physiology plus clinical data; combined-feature classifiers improve pulmonary-complication discrimination over clinical data alone.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classifiers integrate wearable physiological and clinical features for preoperative risk assessment.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Adding physiological data improves AUC, accuracy, F1 and precision over clinical-only models.
evidence.unknown: Prospective patient data and prespecified statistical comparisons support the bounded risk-model result.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning classifiers integrate wearable physiological and clinical features for preoperative risk assessment.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
